vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: token-optimizer
Version: 1.0.18

The OpenClaw Token Optimizer skill bundle is benign. Its code and documentation are entirely focused on optimizing OpenClaw AI costs through model routing, heartbeat configuration, caching, and budget controls. The `CHANGELOG.md` explicitly details significant security improvements, such as the removal of all `subprocess.run` calls in favor of safer `shutil.which` and `urllib.request` for health checks, and defaulting commands to dry-run mode. Instructions for the AI agent in `SKILL.md` and template files (`templates/SOUL.md`, `templates/OPTIMIZATION-RULES.md`) are defensive, guiding the agent towards cost-aware and responsible behavior, rather than attempting prompt injection. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence, or obfuscation.

llm.summary: This skill is meant to reduce OpenClaw costs, but it can persistently change how agents load context, remember sessions, and choose models, so it should be reviewed before installation.

dimensions.detail: Most writes are disclosed under ~/.openclaw, with local backups, templates, prompts, config, and stats; analyzer also writes a local analysis file in the current directory, and health checks may contact localhost, LM Studio, Ollama, or Groq endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has no runtime dependencies, no install-time script behavior beyond standard packaging metadata, and no evidence of obfuscated or remote payload execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad triggers such as "save money" and generated rules such as loading only selected files and not auto-loading prior messages or previous tool outputs; those instructions are under-scoped for a global agent prompt even though they are cost-related.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent OpenClaw config, workspace templates, prompt-rule files, backups, and stats; config rollback exists, but prompt and memory-behavior changes are global and not clearly reversible or consent-gated beyond running --apply and manually adding prompt rules.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The cost-optimization purpose is coherent with model routing, caching, heartbeats, budgets, and context reduction, but the generated prompt files go beyond configuration tuning by creating global future-session operating rules for agent context loading, memory updates, and model choice.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want this tool to change OpenClaw cost behavior and are comfortable reviewing generated files before adding them to an agent prompt. Pay particular attention to the prompt rules that suppress prior context, choose cheaper models by default, and write daily memory notes; keep copies of existing prompts and remove generated rules if they degrade safety or correctness.
llm.findings:
[T01] expected: Accepted as a material review concern: the generated prompt rules are disclosed and cost-related, but they persistently alter future agent context loading and memory behavior across sessions.
[LP3] unexpected: Partly accepted: the docs disclose the paths and capabilities, but no explicit least-privilege permission scope is present for config, prompt, local file, and network access.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: generic triggers such as "save money" and "too expensive" can activate this configuration-changing skill in unrelated cost discussions.
[TR2] unexpected: Accepted in context with SQP-1: the trigger wording is broad enough to be ambiguous around ordinary save or cost language.
[SQP-2] expected: Mixed: provider reachability checks are expected for heartbeat verification, and setup-heartbeat still routes through dry-run-aware save_config; however dry-run paths can still create local directories and verification can mutate local stats.
[SDI-1] expected: Partly accepted: local analysis output, stats tracking, and prompt/template generation are related to reporting and optimization, but prompt generation materially expands the behavior users must review.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a scope concern: generated instructions for session initialization, selective recall, and memory updates are cost-related but persistently affect later agent behavior.
[SSRF2] expected: Downgraded: localhost and configured provider GET requests are health checks with no request bodies or credentials observed, but users should expect those endpoints to be contacted during health or verification commands.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: no cron, startup service, or backdoor persistence was found; the persistence is local config, backups, prompt files, workspace templates, and stats disclosed by the skill.
[SQP-3] expected: Accepted as a quality and control concern: defaulting to Haiku is central to cost savings, but the generated prompt language is strong and global, with limited user override language.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Partly accepted: donation messaging and verify_count updates are not core verification behavior, though they remain local and are not evidence of malicious activity.
